pNone_chapter_1: Byomkesh Bakshi stands in a dimly lit hallway of a colonial-era hospital, holding a black rotary telephone receiver to his ear. He wears a crisp white dhoti and kurta with a dark shawl draped over his shoulders, his expression focused and sharp as he listens to the caller. Beside him, Ajit leans against the pale green plaster wall, watching his friend with an observant and curious gaze. The scene is illuminated by the cool, sterile glow of an overhead lamp, casting long shadows across the checkered floor tiles. Outside the tall windows, the evening mist of Kolkata begins to settle over the courtyard.
